unit: Approval Gate check 5 (latest-version) vs the Approvals register
description: Every PENDING approval references the highest draft version that exists for its action.
why_it_exists: The gate refuses at decision time when a newer draft exists (STALE, 'Approve that one instead'), but a register full of PENDING approvals pointing at superseded drafts means the owner is repeatedly offered decisions that cannot be actioned. The census pairs each pending approval's draft_version with latest_version_for_action to make the gap visible before the owner hits it.

expect.approvals_pending_detail: for every PENDING approval, draft_version equals latest_version_for_action
expect.latest_version_for_action: max(parseInt(version)) over all Drafts rows sharing that action_id
expect.no_orphan_drafts: every PENDING approval's draft_id resolves to a Drafts row (never '(no draft row)')

assertions: For each PENDING approval, the version of the draft it names equals the maximum version recorded for that approval's action_id.
Every PENDING approval's draft_id matches an existing Drafts row.
An approval whose draft_version is behind the latest is stale by construction and must be SUPERSEDED rather than left decidable.

The gate's own STALE checks (content_hash equality against token_hash_or_reference, and latest-version-in-chain) must still fire independently at decision time; this invariant is about register hygiene, not a replacement for them.
target_unresolved_reason: kind is "invariant": not executed by harness/run.js.
